Line: Year one: seven teams, a snake draft, and a title nobody could settle. Mike's Bad Attitude Gang and Josh Lavrinc's Jefferson Juggernauts split it as the league's first co-champions.
Four new owners (Dave, Todd, Johnson and Jimmy Crisan) and the league's first outright champion: Jeff Grace's Pardon the Intoxication.
The last snake draft ever, and Jimmy Crisan's Warren Brownies close out the founding era with the trophy.
The auction arrives and the Wild West begins. Twelve teams, two conferences, and Todd's Fightin Ferrets edge Dave's Kardiac Kids 130–122 for his first title.
Sixteen teams and the original divisions. Brian and Ron's Swissvale Flashes start a back-to-back run, beating rookie BJ Funari in the final.
Note: Four rookies: BJ, Jon/Rick, Marcus Ruby, Sean Ritson.

Line: Mike goes 12–1, posts the year's top score and a 127.5-point blowout… and watches Brian and Ron repeat. ONE HOUSE DIVIDED beat Jeff Grace 110.5–79.
Third season, first title: Jon and Rick's Prodigal Sons roll the Silver Bullets 124–83.
Note: Jake paid $94 for LaDainian Tomlinson, still the most ever for a running back.

Line: One of the final years of the Wild West era: Tony Trozzo and Happy Valley Hammer Time take down his dad's Fightin Ferrets for the first of his back-to-back titles.
New divisions (Kardashian and Lautner), same champ. Tony repeats, 104–89.5 over Josh Lavrinc, as the Wild West auction rides off into the sunset.
The Golden Wiggins draft era opens, and Jake's Jagoffs win it all by one point, 107–106 over the Silver Bullets.
Seven years after losing the first auction-era final, Dave's Kardiac Kids finally get theirs: 132–113 over Brian and Ron.
Note: Matt Brown paid $96 for Aaron Rodgers, still the league record.

Line: The one-and-done Pop-Star divisions, and Chris Johnson's V-Unit edge the Prodigal Sons 107.44–102.68 for his first ring.
Note: Rookies Dan Reilly and Ed Peters arrive.

Line: Cuoco, Kunis, Stone and Upton take over the divisions, and Joe's Reindeers win his first title, 89.8–82.08. The Prodigal Sons lose a second straight final.
Ten years after his first, Todd wins title number two, 128.82–89.98 over Mike's Bad Attitude Gang.
Fourteen years after sharing one, Mike wins a title all his own: Bad Attitude Gang 137.98, BJ's Motown Moonshiners 131.08.
Tony's third ring, and it isn't close: Happy Valley Hammer Time 133, the V-Unit 69.26.
Joe's second title, 155.46–120.48 over Mike, who loses his second final in four years.
Note: Josh Lavrinc dropped 176.72 on Todd in Week 11.

Line: Two finals lost, then BJ's turn: the Fort Myers Sunshiners win it, 143.46–93 over Dave, in the last Golden Wiggins draft.
The draft goes remote, and Johnson's V-Unit win a second title, 149.68–113.32 over Tony.
Note: Josh Farber's one season produced a $1 Justin Jefferson.

Line: Ten years after his first, Jake wins again, 138.86–83.02 over Camp Kes. It's Josh Lavrinc's last season, nineteen years after his co-title.
Brian and Ron go 12–2 and reach the final. The Prodigal Sons take title number two anyway, 140.4–93.46.
In his tenth season, Bob Keslar wins it: Camp Kes over Hadley's Comets, who lose a second straight final.
Joe's third title closes the 16-team era: Reindeer 129.66, Fetrow's Southside Shooters 81.88.
Note: Todd beat Fetrow by 106.24 in Week 11.

Line: Two tiers, 21 teams, Superflex. The Prodigal Sons win their third title over Joe, while Mike takes the Lower tier and earns his way back up.
Note: Joe's 221 in Week 12 is the highest score in league history.
